did.abstract: Peter Carroll (1943-2024) was an author, historian, educator, and co-chair of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives. The Peter Carroll Papers (1930-2024) include documents created and collected by Peter Carroll, including administrative documents related to the Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives (ALBA) and Veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade (VALB) organizations; written works and research files on individual veterans, as well as subjects related to the Spanish Civil War and the U.S. government's treatment of soldiers; and oral history recordings and transcripts.
did.langmaterial: Materials are primarily in English and Spanish, with some materials in French, German, Russian, and Dutch.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Donated by Peter N. Carroll in 2011, 2018, December 2021, and June 2024, and by Peter Carroll's children in January 2025. The accession numbers associated with these gifts are 2011.021, 2018.132, 2021.092, 2024.037, and 2025.016.

appraisal.head: Appraisal
appraisal.p: In 2026 during processing, 1 linear foot of publications, duplicate materials, and student work were deaccesioned; 25 commercial video recordings and 2 commercial audio recordings were deaccessioned; and 18 commercial, duplicate, or corrupted born-digital carriers were deaccessioned.
In November 2026, five additional VHS tapes and 2 DVD-Rs were deaccessioned due to duplicative and commercial content.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The records are arranged in three series, with one further arranged in subseries. The series and subseries arrangement of the records is as follows:
Series I. Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives Administrative Files, arranged chronologically;
Series II. Spanish Civil War Research Files;
Series II.A Written Works, arranged alphabetically;
Series II.B Research Files, arranged alphabetically;
Series III. Oral History Interviews, arranged alphabetically.

bioghist.head: Biographical Note
bioghist.p: Peter Carroll (1943-2024) was an author, historian, educator, and co-chair of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives. Starting in the mid-1970s, Carroll developed relationships with several members of the Veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade (VALB). He was deeply involved with the Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives (ALBA) since the organization's creation in the late 1970s, serving as chair of the Board of Governors from 1994-2010 and 2018-2020, and on the Executive Committee. He also served as co-editor of The Volunteer, co-curated several exhibits, and taught workshops on the Spanish Civil War to educators and students. Carroll conducted extensive research with members of VALB and worked to preserve their stories. Alongside his work with ALBA, he also chaired the Advisory Committee of the Puffin Foundation and advised on the Activist Gallery of the Museum of the City of New York.

Carroll authored and edited more than 20 books, including The Odyssey of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade: Americans in the Spanish Civil War (1994) and They Still Draw Pictures: Children's Art in Wartime from the Spanish Civil War to Kosovo (2002), co-authored with Anthony L. Geist. He also frequently wrote newspaper articles on subjects related to the Spanish Civil War and the Abraham Lincoln Brigade.
Faber, Sebastiaan. "In Memoriam: Peter Neil Carroll (1943-2024)." The Volunteer, Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives, 18 Sept. 2024, albavolunteer.org/2024/09/peter-neil-carroll-1943-2024/.

phystech.head: Born-Digital Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Advance notice is required for the use of computer records. Original physical digital media is restricted. An access terminal for born-digital materials in the collection is available by appointment for reading room viewing and listening only. Researchers may view an item's original container and/or carrier, but the physical carriers themselves are not available for use because of preservation concerns.

phystech.head: Audiovisual Access Policies and Procedures
phystech.p: Audiovisual materials have not been preserved and may not be available to researchers. Materials not yet digitized will need to have access copies made before they can be used. To request an access copy, or if you are unsure if an item has been digitized, please contact NYU Special Collections (special.collections@nyu.edu, 212-998-2596) with the collection name, collection number, and a description of the item(s) requested. A staff member will respond to you with further information.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Suggested format for citing materials in a collection:
Identification of item, date; Peter Carroll Papers; ALBA 281; box number; folder number or item identifier; Tamiment Library/Robert F. Wagner Labor Archives, New York University.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Processing decisions made prior to 2018 have not been recorded. At the time of accessioning, materials associated with Accession number 2018.132 were rehoused in acid-free folders and archival boxes. Born-digital items were separated from the material, boxed, labeled, and inventoried.

In 2024, an accretion of research materials and writings were rehoused in archival boxes, maintaining original order and retaining original folders, except in the case of loose materials. These materials were added to the collection's inventory.

In September 2026, this collection was arranged and described by an archivist. Paper materials were placed in acid-free folders in manuscript boxes, oversized materials were foldered and housed appropriately according to their size, and rusty paperclips and staples were removed. Audiovisual materials were placed in format-appropriate housing. Paper, audiovisual, and born-digital materials were arranged intellectually and their description was integrated.

In 2026, born-digital carriers containing data were forensically imaged, analyzed, and arranged in Forensic Toolkit. The born-digital audio and video recordings were arranged separately in directories on locally-mounted networked storage and intellectually integrated into appropriate series. New York University Libraries follow professional standards and best practices when imaging, ingesting, and processing born-digital material in order to maintain the integrity and authenticity of the content.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Peter Carroll Papers (1930-2024) include documents created and collected by Peter Carroll. The collection is comprised of administrative records of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives (ALBA) and Veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade (VALB) organizations, as well as Carroll's personal research files on the Spanish Civil War.

Administrative documents of ALBA in this collection include notes and agendas from the Board of Governors and Executive Committee, financial documents, event ephemera and planning files, recordings of events, issues of their journal The Volunteer (and of its predecessor, The Volunteer for Liberty), teaching materials on the Spanish Civil War, documentation of archival acquisitions, and files of the Bay Area chapter. This collection also includes VALB files, such as event ephemera and project documentation. Events represented in this collection include anniversary dinners and gatherings from 1976-2002, Spanish Civil War anniversary commemoration gatherings and ceremonies, monument dedication ceremonies, memorial services, film screenings, book talks, and exhibitions.

Carroll's research files on the Spanish Civil War include written works by himself and other authors, notes and primary sources used in the writing of his book The Odyssey of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade: Americans in the Spanish Civil War (1994), notes and documents collected on individual veterans and subjects, and oral history recordings and transcripts. Subjects that Carroll collected materials on include court proceedings related to the House Committee on Un-American Activities (HUAC) and the Subversive Activities Control Act (SACA), discrimination faced by American soldiers, discrimination by the American government of ALB veterans, and deserters of the International Brigades. His research files also include document scans with accompanying notes and correspondence from Special Collections in Moscow, documents requested from the FBI via the Freedom of Information Act, and audiovisual recordings on the Spanish Civil War collected by Carroll.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The Tamiment Library and Robert F. Wagner Labor Archives is not authorized to grant permission to publish or reproduce materials from Series III, Oral History Interviews. Materials in this series are for use in the reading room only.

This collection is protected by copyright and/or related rights. You are free to use materials in the collection in any way that is permitted by the copyright and related rights legislation that applies to your use. For other uses you need to obtain permission from the rights-holder(s).

Any rights (including copyright and related rights to publicity and privacy) held by Peter N. Carroll over audiovisual materials in the collection were relinquished and transferred to the public domain in February 2017 by Peter N. Carroll. scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series I. Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives Administrative Files (1937-2024) includes files related to the Abraham Lincoln Brigade Archives (ALBA) and the Veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade (VALB) as organizations. This series contains administrative files such as documents of the Board of Governors, applications for funding, budget documents, administrative correspondence, and files of the ALBA Bay Area chapter. This series also contains issues of ALBA's journal, The Volunteer (formerly known as The Volunteer for Liberty), as well as submissions, drafts, and correspondence with readers; documentation of VALB projects and campaigns such as the Nicaraguan Ambulance Project and the Nicaraguan Wheelchair Repair Project, during which veterans fundraised to provide aid to those affected by the Nicaraguan Revolution; and teaching materials on the Spanish Civil War, including the professional development workshop "America and World Fascism: From the Spanish Civil War to Nuremberg and Beyond," which was taught online and across the Northeast United States.

Event files in this series contain planning documentation, such as correspondence, meeting minutes, travel itineraries, and event contracts; ephemera, such as flyers, pamphlets, playbills, and postcards; photographs; and recordings of ALBA and VALB events. Events in this series include anniversary dinners and gatherings from 1976-2002; Spanish Civil War anniversary commemoration gatherings and ceremonies; monument dedication ceremonies; memorial services; film screenings; and exhibitions, such as "Barcelona: The Forgotten Olympics of 1936" (1992), "Shouts from the Wall" (1994-2002), "The Aura of the Cause" (1997), "Drawings of the Spanish Civil War: Luis Quintanilla" (1999), "They Still Draw Pictures: Children's Art in Wartime" (2000), "Facing Fascism: New York and the Spanish Civil War" (2005), "Ralph Falsanella: Artist of the People" (2006), and "Art and Politics: Posters from the Spanish Civil War, 1936-1939" (2007).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series III. Oral History Interviews (1977-1999) includes audio recordings and transcripts of Spanish Civil War veteran interviews, as well as administrative files and press clippings for the Radical Elders Oral History Project. Interviews with Eluard Luchelle McDaniels and Vaughn Love were conducted by Peter Carroll for the Radical Elders Oral History Project. Other interviews in the series are not labeled with a specific project, and some were likely conducted by Carroll for research during the writing of The Odyssey of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade: Americans in the Spanish Civil War.

bioghist.head: Historical Note
bioghist.p: The Radical Elders Oral History Project was created in the San Francisco Bay Area in the 1970s and continued until 1981. The project was a collaboration between leftist activists from older and younger generations, and many veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade were involved, including Peter Carroll and Milt Wolff. The group produced over a dozen audio interviews, and were featured in radio programs and events in the Bay Area.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This series is arranged alphabetically by the interviewee's last name. Tapes not labeled with a name are arranged together at the end of the list.
